items.question: What invulnerability to physical harm arises for one whose mind is absorbed in that state?
premises: A person may be subjected to cutting.
Absorption in that state directs the mind away from the body.
Mental fixation on that state alters the experience of bodily injury.
items.inference: One who has gone to that state and whose mind is fixed on it is not truly cut even while being cut.
uncertainties: The referent of 'that' (tad) depends on the preceding verses and is not explicit in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: One who has reached that state and whose mind is fixed on it, though being cut, is not cut.
